elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, etc.)
sub_elements.evidence: id: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; grant OT2OD032701; publication doi: 10.1007/s12028-024-02007
sub_elements.quality_note: The dataset id is only the project homepage URL, not a persistent dataset identifier. No dataset-level DOI or RRID is present (the DOI cited belongs to a methods paper, and OT2OD032701 is a grant number).

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI; description spans purpose, scale (20 centers, 100,000+ patients), modalities, standards, and August 2025 status counts
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear title plus a comprehensive multi-hundred-character description covering purpose, scope, modalities, and current dataset statistics.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [CHoRUS, Bridge2AI, critical care, OMOP Common Data Model, EHR, waveform telemetry, DICOM, EEG, health equity, ICU, ...] (26 keywords)
sub_elements.quality_note: 26 relevant keywords covering domain, methods, modalities, standards, and conditions.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Landing Page or Platform URL
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://chorus4ai.org/
sub_elements.quality_note: Dedicated landing page URL where users can learn about the dataset and access process.

sub_elements.name: Associated Project or Program
sub_elements.evidence: keywords include Bridge2AI; external_resources: Bridge2AI Program (https://bridge2ai.org/chorus), AIM-AHEAD Training Program
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear association with the NIH Bridge2AI program and AIM-AHEAD partnership.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Mechanism Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: 'distributed under controlled access requiring institutional email registration and signed licensing agreement. Access granted after review and approval process.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Controlled/registered access model clearly defined, including the registration and approval workflow.

sub_elements.name: Data Use Agreement Required?
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: 'signed licensing agreement... complete registration form with name, institutional email... users receive email with access instructions'; access contacts dbold@emory.edu, jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org
sub_elements.quality_note: DUA requirement stated explicitly with concrete steps and named access-request contacts.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distributions each list path: https://chorus4ai.org/ (secure enclave, controlled access); access instructions provided upon approval
sub_elements.quality_note: Platform access point provided for all five distributions (secure enclave via chorus4ai.org). Not direct download links, but access route is defined.

sub_elements.name: File Formats Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: OMOP CDM, WFDB, DICOM, OHNLP-tokenized text (TXT/text/plain), EDF+ and Persyst
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific file formats named for every modality.

sub_elements.name: External Links to Similar or Related Datasets
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: OHDSI/OMOP CDM (ohdsi.org), Bridge2AI Program, GitHub org (chorus-ai, 28 repos), NIH RePORTER project details
sub_elements.quality_note: Multiple external resource links to related standards, repositories, and program resources.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.evidence: license: 'Controlled Access - Data Use Agreement Required (OT2OD032701)'; ip_restrictions: GitHub repos use MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses; data reuse governed by DUA and NIH grant terms
sub_elements.quality_note: License terms clearly stated (controlled access for data, MIT/Apache-2.0 for software). Reuse is permitted within DUA terms.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized
sub_elements.evidence: OMOP Common Data Model, WFDB (PhysioNet), DICOM, EDF+, Persyst, OHNLP tokenization
sub_elements.quality_note: All modalities standardized to widely recognized formats/standards.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: cleaning_strategies: 'validated against published metadata schemas (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, OHNLP, EDF+, Persyst)'; preproc: OMOP CDM transformation enabling OHDSI tool stack
sub_elements.quality_note: Explicit conformance to multiple community schemas/data models.

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Defined for Linking
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit participant ID scheme or cross-modality linking key described; only aggregate admission counts (45,000 unique admissions, 50,000 admissions) are given
sub_elements.quality_note: No linking identifiers or key structure documented for joining records across modalities.

sub_elements.name: Documentation of Processing Tools for Reproducibility
sub_elements.evidence: chorus-mapping repository, chorus_waveform repository, privacy_scan_tool, DeGauss/UF-Geocoding, OHNLP toolkit, GitHub org chorus-ai (28 repositories)
sub_elements.quality_note: Named repositories and tools for mapping, waveform standardization, privacy scanning, and geocoding support reproducibility.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review Documented
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: 'approved through institutional review board processes at all 14 data acquisition centers'; community-facing ethics focus groups
sub_elements.quality_note: IRB oversight documented across all acquisition sites, plus community ethics engagement.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified: 'EHR data de-identified through OMOP CDM transformation and privacy scanning tools (privacy_scan_tool)... OHNLP tokenization... DICOM header de-identification'
sub_elements.quality_note: Modality-specific de-identification methods described, tied to HIPAA/institutional requirements.

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Removed or Masked
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified references removing 'patient identifiable information from image metadata' and tokenizing notes, but no enumerated list of identifiers (names, dates, SSNs, MRNs) removed
sub_elements.quality_note: De-identification is described in general terms but the specific identifiers removed or masked are not enumerated.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent: 'Retrospective data collection... using waiver of individual consent framework approved by IRBs at participating institutions'
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent framework explicitly documented (IRB-approved waiver for retrospective data), which is the appropriate procedure for this data type.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Sourcing Statement Included
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research and at_risk_populations describe ethical governance, community ethics focus groups, and patient-focused ethics pillar; description states 'ethically sourced'
sub_elements.quality_note: Strong ethical sourcing narrative including vulnerable-population protections and community engagement.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Population Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: instances and subpopulations: critically ill patients in ICU/PICU/NICU across 14 hospitals within 20 academic centers
sub_elements.quality_note: Population and subpopulation characteristics described with setting and institutional distribution.

sub_elements.name: Number of Participants or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: 'over 45,000 unique admissions', '50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU', target 'exceeds 100,000 critically ill patients'
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific counts reported for current release and target enrollment.

sub_elements.name: Modalities or Data Types Listed
sub_elements.evidence: structured EHR (OMOP), waveform telemetry (WFDB), medical imaging (DICOM), EEG (EDF+/Persyst), clinical notes (OHNLP)
sub_elements.quality_note: All five modalities clearly enumerated with formats.

sub_elements.name: Conditions or Phenotypes Represented
sub_elements.evidence: Focus is on 'acute and critical illness' broadly; no specific condition groups or phenotype breakdown enumerated
sub_elements.quality_note: Only the general clinical context (critical/acute illness) is given; no specific disease conditions or phenotype groupings are represented.

sub_elements.name: File Dimensions or Sampling Rates Provided
sub_elements.evidence: '1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data', '23 TB of waveform data', '7,642 admissions with radiology data', '1,000 images currently available'
sub_elements.quality_note: Substantial dataset dimensions and volumes provided per modality (row counts, TB, image/admission counts), though acquisition sampling rates are not stated.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit version number; only 'Current release (August 2025)' is referenced
sub_elements.quality_note: No semantic dataset version number (e.g., 1.0) is provided.

sub_elements.name: Version History Documented
sub_elements.evidence: No release_notes or change log present; updates describes ongoing expansion but not discrete versions
sub_elements.quality_note: No version history or release notes documented.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions for Each Version
sub_elements.evidence: No per-version change descriptions present
sub_elements.quality_note: No changelog of specific changes between versions.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.evidence: updates: 'Dataset updated continuously as data collection progresses at 14 acquisition centers... Project timeline extends through November 30, 2026'; status tracked via GitHub project management
sub_elements.quality_note: Continuous update cadence and project timeline explicitly stated.

sub_elements.name: Versioned Documentation or External References
sub_elements.evidence: version_access: 'Dataset versions accessible through secure enclave with controlled access... Version history maintained as data collection expands from 45K to target 100K+'; NIH RePORTER and GitHub org links
sub_elements.quality_note: Version-access mechanism described and backed by external references (NIH RePORTER, GitHub org).

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Rationale for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes and addressing_gaps: 'improving recovery from acute illness', 'Lack of diverse multi-center critical care datasets', 'Insufficient data standardization'
sub_elements.quality_note: Rich motivation and explicitly enumerated research gaps addressed.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objective or Task
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: characterize acute/critical illness, predict complications, measure treatment response, external validation, label prediction targets; intended_uses: AI/ML model development
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific ML/AI research tasks and objectives clearly stated.

sub_elements.name: Funding Source or Grant Agency Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program... administered by NIH Office of the Director'
sub_elements.quality_note: Funding agency clearly identified.

sub_elements.name: Award Number or Grant ID Present
sub_elements.evidence: 'National Institutes of Health grant OT2OD032701 (project number 1OT2OD032701-01)... Opportunity Number: OTA-21-008... Assistance Listing Number: 93.310'
sub_elements.quality_note: Precise award number plus rich supplementary grant metadata (opportunity number, study section, funding amount, dates).

sub_elements.name: Acknowledgement of Platform or Participant Support
sub_elements.evidence: funders detail NIH support; existing_uses and external_resources acknowledge AIM-AHEAD partnership and contributing centers; maintainers acknowledge consortium sites
sub_elements.quality_note: Support from NIH, AIM-AHEAD, and contributing institutions is acknowledged, though no dedicated acknowledgements field.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Setting or Sites Described
sub_elements.evidence: data_collectors: '14 data acquisition centers across 20 academic institutions'; maintainers name MGH (lead), University of Florida, UT Health Science Center, Tufts Medicine
sub_elements.quality_note: Collection settings and lead institutions described with specificity.

sub_elements.name: Data Capture Method or Device Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: bedside monitors via gateway/middleware (waveform), hospital PACS (imaging), EHR systems with OMOP transformation, hospital EEG databases
sub_elements.quality_note: Capture methods and source devices/systems described per modality.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing or Cleaning Steps Documented
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies (OMOP transformation, OHNLP tokenization, WFDB standardization, DICOM de-id, re-id-limiting transforms) and cleaning_strategies (validated semantic mappings, schema compliance validation)
sub_elements.quality_note: Detailed, modality-specific preprocessing and cleaning pipeline documented.

sub_elements.name: Open-Source Processing Code Provided
sub_elements.evidence: chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, privacy_scan_tool, DeGauss/UF-Geocoding; GitHub org chorus-ai with 28 repositories at https://github.com/chorus-ai
sub_elements.quality_note: Named processing code repositories and public GitHub organization provided.

sub_elements.name: External Standards or References Cited
sub_elements.evidence: Neurocritical Care publication doi: 10.1007/s12028-024-02007; standards OMOP, DICOM, WFDB (PhysioNet), OHNLP, EDF+
sub_elements.quality_note: Peer-reviewed publication and multiple external standards cited.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Limitations Section Present
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: 'Dataset still actively growing and not yet complete', 'Controlled access restricts open research'
sub_elements.quality_note: Explicit limitations documented with concrete detail about incomplete modalities and access constraints.

sub_elements.name: Sampling Bias or Representativeness Noted
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: 'Academic medical center population bias' and 'Retrospective data collection bias' with discussion of representativeness relative to community/rural settings
sub_elements.quality_note: Sampling biases and representativeness explicitly discussed.

sub_elements.name: Quality Control or Validation Steps Mentioned
sub_elements.evidence: cleaning_strategies: 'Schema compliance validation across all modalities', 'Cross-site data quality checks through CHoRUSReports characterization reports'; labeling QC via Chorus_SOP
sub_elements.quality_note: QC and validation procedures described (schema validation, characterization reports, SOP-based review).

sub_elements.name: Known Risks or Use Constraints Listed
sub_elements.evidence: discouraged_uses (clinical decisions without validation, re-identification), prohibited_uses (re-identification, redistribution), future_use_impacts (risk of algorithmic bias propagation)
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear constraints, discouraged/prohibited uses, and downstream risk of bias propagation documented.

sub_elements.name: Conflicts of Interest Declared
sub_elements.evidence: No conflicts-of-interest statement present in the datasheet
sub_elements.quality_note: No COI declaration provided.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: 'CHoRUS Consortium / Massachusetts General Hospital'; access via a self-hosted Azure-based secure enclave rather than a recognized public repository (PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo)
sub_elements.quality_note: Distributed through a project-controlled secure enclave, not a recognized third-party data platform, though it follows PhysioNet/OMOP conventions.

sub_elements.name: Cross-referenced DOIs or Related Dataset Links
sub_elements.evidence: Neurocritical Care publication doi: 10.1007/s12028-024-02007; NIH RePORTER project-details link (10472824)
sub_elements.quality_note: Cross-referenced publication DOI and federal grant record provided.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Reference
sub_elements.evidence: OMOP Common Data Model / OHDSI, DICOM, WFDB (PhysioNet), OHNLP, EDF+/Persyst
sub_elements.quality_note: Strong alignment with multiple community data standards and consortia.

sub_elements.name: Associated Outreach Materials
sub_elements.evidence: AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI Clinical Care Training Program (Jupyter notebooks, workshops); Chorus_SOP documentation site with interactive workflow diagrams; GitHub documentation
sub_elements.quality_note: Outreach and training materials, tutorials, and SOP documentation referenced.

sub_elements.name: Similar Dataset Links or Thematic Grouping
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: Bridge2AI Program 'supporting AI-ready biomedical datasets across four data generation projects at https://bridge2ai.org/chorus'
sub_elements.quality_note: Thematic grouping within the Bridge2AI family of data generation projects is explicit.

strengths: Exceptional technical transparency: modality-specific acquisition, preprocessing, and cleaning pipelines with named open-source repositories (chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, privacy_scan_tool) and a public GitHub organization with 28 repositories
Complete funding transparency with precise NIH award metadata (OT2OD032701 / 1OT2OD032701-01, opportunity number, study section, funding amount, and project dates)
Well-documented ethical governance including IRB approval at all 14 sites, waiver-of-consent framework, community ethics focus groups, and explicit vulnerable-population protections
Strong limitations and risk disclosure covering academic-center and retrospective sampling bias, QC/validation via CHoRUSReports, and downstream algorithmic-bias propagation risk
Rich composition detail with concrete scale metrics (45,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 23 TB waveform data) across five clearly enumerated modalities
weaknesses: No persistent dataset identifier (DOI/RRID) - the id field is only the project homepage URL
Provenance and version tracking is the weakest area: no version number, no release notes, and no per-version change history
No linking-identifier scheme documented for joining records across modalities
Dataset is distributed via a self-hosted secure enclave rather than a recognized public repository, and specific de-identified condition/phenotype groups are not enumerated
recommendations: Mint a persistent dataset DOI (e.g., via DataCite or a repository) distinct from the methods-paper DOI and record it in the id/doi field
Add explicit version numbers, release notes, and per-release change descriptions to support reproducibility and citation of specific dataset snapshots
Document the participant/admission identifier scheme and cross-modality linking keys used within the enclave
Add a conflicts-of-interest statement for the consortium leadership and contributing institutions
Enumerate the represented condition/phenotype groups and, where feasible, register or mirror the dataset with a recognized platform (e.g., PhysioNet) to strengthen community integration
